Definition: a column (as standing); also a stand, i.e. platform
BiblicalUsage: A pillar in the Bible is something that stands — it holds weight and it marks the way. The LORD went before Israel in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night; the same cloudy pillar came down and stood at the door of the tabernacle while God talked with Moses. In the temple Solomon cast two great pillars of brass, eighteen cubits high, and in the house of Dagon Samson took hold of the two middle pillars and pulled the whole building down.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the pillar is the picture of God's presence going with His people — steady, visible, and impossible to miss. He does not only point the way; He stands in it, ahead of us, so we can follow. And I believe the same God who led by cloud and fire still goes before His people today, even when the pillar looks different than I expect.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea; Samson and Delilah
